# Add a new module

Load `csharp-code-standards` first. Reference module: `Core` (`src/Core/Behind.Core.*`), loaded by the host project `src/Web/Behind.Web`. Smallest complete example: `Quotes` (`src/Quotes/Behind.Quotes.*`, project side `src/Web/Behind.Web.Database.*`): copy its structure for a new module.

## Rules
- Every module gets its own projects under `src/<Module>/`: `Behind.<Module>.Common`, `Behind.<Module>.Domain`, `Behind.<Module>.Database`, `Behind.<Module>.Database.Sqlite`, `Behind.<Module>.Database.Postgres`, `Behind.<Module>.WebApi`, and optionally `Behind.<Module>.Tools` when the module needs a command line tool. The module has no migrator project of its own: the migrator belongs to the project (see the Migrator checklist step).
- The host project (`src/Web/Behind.Web`) loads every module next to the Core module; Core is required and always loaded by default (`AddCore()`/`UseCore()` in `src/Web/Behind.Web/WebApiExtensions.cs`).
- The database is flattened in the project: one database file and one DbContext implements all the context interfaces of every module (Core and the new module) with the use of both the module implementations, never a separate database or DbContext per module. Because of that the project gets its own database migrator project, which applies the migrations of every module into the one database.
- Modules are separate things: a module never references another module (only the Common projects `Behind.Common*`), and only common things (code every module can use) may be added to the Core module; anything specific to one module stays in that module's projects.
- The database context of a module is an interface (the module context interfaces, composed of the `I<Module>...Commands`/`Queries` interfaces), never an abstract base DbContext class that a module requires. The one project DbContext implements the interfaces of every module, so a site can use more than one module at a time without abstract class collisions (a class can implement many interfaces but inherit only one base class).
- A module integrates with Core only through its `ModuleDescriptor` (`Behind.Common.Modules`, defined in `Behind.Common`, so a module never needs a Core reference) and the module interfaces of `Behind.Common.Database` (`IModuleSeed`, `IAuditLabelSource`, `IModuleMigrator`, `AddModuleContext<T>()`). Core already consumes every contribution; a module must not need any change in Core. If something a module needs is missing, add it generically to the Core/Common projects first (with tests) and document it here.
- Module-independent code stays in `src/Common/Behind.Common`, `Behind.Common.Database` and `Behind.Common.WebApi`; only module-specific code goes into the module projects.

## Checklist
1. **Domain** (`src/<Module>/Behind.<Module>.Domain`): immutable records, `VersionedKey<Guid>` ids, no own created/updated columns (see `add-entity`).
2. **Common** (`src/<Module>/Behind.<Module>.Common`): module-specific configuration and helpers, like `Behind.Core.Common`. Generic code goes to `Behind.Common` instead.
3. **Descriptor** (`<Module>Module.Descriptor`, a `ModuleDescriptor` in `Behind.<Module>.Common` or `.WebApi`): the single description of what the module adds to the application (see "What a module contributes" below). `ModuleCatalog.Create` validates it at startup and fails fast.
4. **Database** (`src/<Module>/Behind.<Module>.Database`): the module context interface (`I<Module>Context` exposing the `DbSet`s), `Aggregates/` (`IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>`), `Commands/`, `Queries/`, save results and query extensions, following `Behind.Core.Database`, taking the module context interface (never `AbstractCoreContext`). The module context interface extends `IModuleContext` (`Behind.Common.Database/Modules`: the underlying `DbContext` and `InDeletionState`), which `AbstractCoreContext` implements, so the project context only adds the module `DbSet`s. Web API helpers a module needs (`ManagedListExtensions`, `HoldsGrantAsync`, `PageResponse`) are in `Behind.Common.WebApi`. No abstract DbContext base class. Reuse `Behind.Common.Database` (soft delete, hard delete, restore, auditing, `IUnitOfWork`). Also here: an `IAuditLabelSource` (human readable audit labels for every module entity, see `add-entity`) and an `IModuleSeed` for default data (both optional but registered in `Add<Module>()`).
5. **Providers** (`src/<Module>/Behind.<Module>.Database.Sqlite`, `Behind.<Module>.Database.Postgres`): a design-time only migration context `<Module>ContextSqlite : DbContext`/`<Module>ContextPostgres` that applies only the module model (`modelBuilder.ApplyModuleConfigurations(descriptor.Database...)`) with the history table `descriptor.MigrationsHistoryTable`, the module migrations (`add-ef-migration`) and the design-time factories. Module tables have no foreign keys to Core tables.
6. **Web API** (`src/<Module>/Behind.<Module>.WebApi`): `Add<Module>()`/`Use<Module>()` in `WebApiExtensions` following `Behind.Core.WebApi/WebApiExtensions.cs`: `services.AddModule(<Module>Module.Descriptor)`, the commands/queries, `services.AddModuleContext<I<Module>Context>()`, the `IAuditLabelSource` and `IModuleSeed` registrations; endpoints under `Endpoints/` protected by the module grants (`RequireAuthorization(GrantName.Of(area, action))`, the policies exist already). Embedded frontend files under `Frontend/modules/<key>/` (`GenerateEmbeddedFilesManifest`, `EmbeddedResource Include="Frontend\**\*"`).
7. **Tools (optional)** (`src/<Module>/Behind.<Module>.Tools`): only when the module needs a command line tool. Executable with `System.CommandLine`, `PackAsTool` and a `behind-<module>` `ToolCommandName`, following `Behind.Core.Tools`.
8. **Project** (the host and its database projects):
   - Host `src/Web/Behind.Web`: add the module project reference and call `Add<Module>()`/`Use<Module>()` in `src/Web/Behind.Web/WebApiExtensions.cs` after `AddCore()`/`UseCore()` (order does not matter for the catalog; `UseCore()` serves the frontend files of every registered module).
   - Project database projects (`Behind.<Project>.Database.Sqlite`/`.Postgres`): one context per provider, `class <Project>ContextSqlite(DbContextOptions<<Project>ContextSqlite> options, ModuleCatalog modules) : AbstractCoreContext(options, modules), I<Module>Context` that implements the context interface of every module (one DbSet property each) and applies `ApplyCoreProviderConventions()` plus the provider conventions of the modules. Register with `database.RegisterSqlite<<Project>ContextSqlite>(builder)` and `database.RegisterPostgres<<Project>ContextPostgres>(builder)`; this registers the project context as `AbstractCoreContext`/`IUnitOfWork`, the Core migrator on the plain Core context and the `AccessCatalog`.
   - Project migrator (`Behind.<Project>.Database.Migrator`, referencing `Behind.Core.Database.Migrator`): `Host.CreateApplicationBuilder().AddMigrator((database, host) => database.Register<<Project>ContextSqlite, <Project>ContextPostgres>(host)...)` then `database.RegisterSqliteModule<<Module>ContextSqlite>(host, <Module>Module.Descriptor)` and `RegisterPostgresModule<...>` for every module and registers the module `IModuleSeed`/`IAuditLabelSource` dependencies it needs. `MigratorService` then applies, in order: Core migrations, every `IModuleMigrator`, versioning migrations, built-in users, roles (module grants included), menus (module menu items included) and every `IModuleSeed`.
   - Add all module and project projects to `Behind.slnx`.
9. **Entities**: every entity of the module follows the `add-entity` skill (audit labels through the module `IAuditLabelSource`, soft delete/hard delete/restore with `ModuleDatabase.SoftDeletedEntities`, raw database editor via `add-raw-database-editor` with `ModuleDatabase.ReadOnlyEntities`, management page via `add-management-page`, uploads via `add-vfs-upload`).
10. **Frontend**: pages, viewmodels, views, models and components under `Frontend/modules/<key>/` and RequireJS ids `modules/<key>/...`; locale files `Frontend/modules/<key>/locales/<code>.json` (same format as the Core ones, every language of the Core locales, keys prefixed with the module key); optional css `Frontend/modules/<key>/css/<key>.css` listed in `ModuleFrontend.Styles`. The Core frontend loads `GET /modules`, registers the routes, merges the module messages under the Core ones, adds the styles and shows the administration pages of the modules.
11. **Sites**: update every site (`src/Sites/*`) that should show or configure the module (css, html, configuration, skin).
12. **Tests**: module tests in `tests/Behind.Tests` mirroring the module projects, reusing `Helpers/` test beds (`Helpers/NotesModule.cs` and `Helpers/NotesTestBed.cs` are a complete example of a module descriptor, a flattened context with a module interface, an audit label source and a migration context). Run `dotnet test tests/Behind.Tests/Behind.Tests.csproj` from `Behind/`.
13. **Changelog**: use the `update-changelog` skill.
14. **Docs**: update `Behind/docs/en-US/developer/PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `DOMAIN_MODEL.md` and `WEBAPI_CONVENTIONS.md`, and the user manual of every new page.

## What a module contributes (`ModuleDescriptor`)
| Member | What it does | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Key`, `Name` | lowercase key (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`) used as the frontend namespace `modules/<key>/` and the migration history table `__<key>MigrationsHistory` | unique |
| `GrantAreas` | `ModuleGrantArea(Area, Audience[, Actions])`, actions among `Read/Write/Delete/Manage` (`GrantActions`) | Area `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`, not a Core area. Audience `Everyone` (Administrators all, Users `Read`), `Administration` (Administrators only), `Developer` (Developers `Read`/`Manage`, counts as developer grant). Grants, restrictions, policies, built-in role grants and the grant lists of the Roles and Users pages follow automatically (deterministic ids `Guid.FromName("61000000", "<Area>.<Action>")`) |
| `MenuItems` | `ModuleMenuItem(Id, Title, Url, Position[, Kind, Audience])` ensured in the main menu | stable explicit ids, not the Core ids |
| `AdministrationPages` | `ModuleAdministrationPage(NameKey, Icon, "#/...", Grant)` on the Administration page | the grant must be a module or Core grant; the name is a locale key of the module |
| `Routes` | `ModuleRoute("#/path", "modules/<key>/controllers/<name>"[, Open])` | `Open` routes stay reachable while access is restricted (like sign in) |
| `ConfigurationFiles` | lowercase json file names (`^[a-z][a-z0-9]*\.json$`, unique across modules) such as `markdownviewer.json` | the Settings page shows a tab for every existing file (`ConfigurationFileCatalog.For(root, moduleNames)` is fed by the `ModuleCatalog`); the module loads the file in `Add<Module>()` with `builder.AddReloadableJsonFile(file, true)` and binds its section with `Configure<T>()`/`IOptionsMonitor<T>`, so a settings change applies without a restart; ship a default file in the host project (`Content Update` with `CopyToOutputDirectory`). A module without entities needs no Database projects and leaves `Database` unset (see `src/MarkdownViewer`) |
| `Frontend` | `ModuleFrontend(assembly[, styles])` | embedded `Frontend/` root of the module assembly |
| `Database` | `ModuleDatabase(configurationAssembly) { SoftDeletedEntities, ReadOnlyEntities }` | applied by the project context |

Existing installations pick up a newly added module on the next migrator run: new grants are inserted and added to the built-in roles (edits the administrators made to a built-in role are kept), new menu items are ensured and the module migrations are applied.
